name: Alegría Vineyard
raw_text: Alegría Vineyard is a Zinfandel-dominant field blend, that is 78% Zinfandel, 11% Alicante Bouschet, and 9% Petite Sirah. The remaining 2% includes Carignan, Trousseau (Bastardo), Sangiovese, Negrette, Plavac Mali, Palomino, Syrah, Tannat, Muscat Noir, Monbadon, Peloursin, Graciano, Cinsaut, Béclan, and Grenache. The vineyard is planted on Goldridge sandy loam soils with good drainage. Head-trained and dry-farmed, the vines average over 100 years old. The old gnarly vines produce intensely concentrated fruit with complex spice and dark berry flavors. Head-trained, dry-farmed. Sandy loam soils (Goldridge series). Vine age: 100+ years. Dense, concentrated fruit with pepper and bramble notes.

name: Monte Rosso Vineyard
historical_producers: Italian Swiss Colony, Louis M. Martini
raw_text: One of California's most historic vineyards, Monte Rosso sits at 1,100–1,500 feet elevation on red volcanic soils derived from ancient lava flows – the name means 'Red Mountain.' The vineyard is predominantly Zinfandel (55%) with Cabernet Sauvignon (20%) and Petite Sirah (15%). The remaining 10% is a mix of Alicante Bouschet, Grenache, and Carignan. The thin, rocky volcanic soils force the vines to dig deep, producing small, intensely flavored clusters. Head-trained vines planted in the 1880s continue to produce today. Volcanic red soils, rocky, shallow. Elevation 1100-1500 ft. Head-trained, dry-farmed. Very old-vine Zinfandel.

name: Bedrock Vineyard
raw_text: Bedrock Vineyard, originally planted by William Hood in the 1880s, is a true California field blend with Zinfandel (62%) dominating alongside Alicante Bouschet (14%), Petite Sirah (8%), Carignane (7%), and a host of other varieties comprising the remaining 9% including Grenache, Mourvedre, Cinsaut, and Peloursin. The soils are a mix of clay loam and well-drained gravel benchland soils. The vineyard has been farmed organically and the old vines demonstrate remarkable resilience and complexity. Clay loam and gravel. Benchland. Organic farming. Mixed field blend. Vine age 100+ years.

name: Pagani Ranch
raw_text: The Pagani Ranch is an exceptional old-vine Zinfandel site with vines dating to the 1880s. The vineyard is a classic field blend: Zinfandel (70%) is by far the dominant variety, complemented by Alicante Bouschet (12%), Petite Sirah (10%), and smaller amounts of Carignan (4%) and other varieties (4%) including Barbera, Grenache and Cinsaut. The soils are a well-drained sandy loam over a clay subsoil. The interplanting of different varieties reflects the traditional Italian approach to field blending, ensuring ripening continuity across vintages. Sandy loam over clay subsoil. Head-trained. Classic Italian field blend approach. Dry-farmed.

name: Teldeschi Ranch
raw_text: Teldeschi Ranch in Dry Creek Valley is planted on classic benchland soils—well-drained sandy loam over gravelly sub-soils. The ranch was planted in the early 1900s and is predominantly Zinfandel at approximately 80%, making it a TTB-labeled Zinfandel vineyard. The remaining 20% is a mix of Petite Sirah (10%), Carignan (6%), and other field varieties (4%). Dry Creek's warm days and cool nights create the ideal conditions for these old-vine Zinfandels, resulting in wines of concentration, spice, and fruit complexity. Sandy loam over gravel benchland soils. Dry Creek Valley benchland. Warm days, cool nights.

name: Marston Family Vineyard
raw_text: Perched high on Spring Mountain, the Marston Family Vineyard sits atop shallow, rocky volcanic soils with fractured volcanic rock and decomposed granite. The site is planted predominantly to Cabernet Sauvignon (85%), with Merlot (8%) and Cabernet Franc (7%). The mountain soils stress the vines naturally, producing small berries with thick skins and concentrated tannins. The vineyard's elevation of 1,800 feet creates long growing seasons with significant diurnal temperature variation. Volcanic rock, decomposed granite, shallow soils. Elevation 1,800 ft. Cabernet-dominant. Significant diurnal variation.

name: St. George Vineyard
raw_text: One of the oldest continuously producing vineyards in Napa Valley, planted on the deep alluvial gravel loams of the Rutherford Bench. The vineyard is primarily Cabernet Sauvignon (76%) with Merlot (14%), Cabernet Franc (6%), and Petit Verdot (4%). The Rutherford Bench's famous 'Rutherford Dust' character comes from these well-drained gravelly loam over clay loam soils. Old vines show remarkable longevity in these deep, fertile soils. Deep alluvial gravelly loam over clay loam (Bale clay). Famous 'Rutherford Dust' character. Well-drained benchland.

name: Evangelho Vineyard
raw_text: The Evangelho Vineyard is an extraordinary survivor from the pre-Prohibition era. The vineyard grows on deep windblown sandy soils (Antioch series), which are phylloxera-resistant by nature—most vines here are own-rooted. The field blend is centered on Zinfandel (65%), Mourvedre (15%), Alicante Bouschet (10%), and a mix of Carignan, Muscat Noir, Cinsaut, Grenache, and Palomino for the remaining 10%. The sandy soils mean the vines are largely phylloxera-free and have never been replanted. Deep sandy soils (Antioch series), own-rooted vines, phylloxera-resistant. Warm, dry climate moderated by Delta breezes.

name: Tofanelli Vineyard
raw_text: The Tofanelli Vineyard is planted on Calistoga's benchland volcanic-influenced soils, a mix of stony loam and well-drained alluvial fans at the base of Mount St. Helena. The vineyard features Zinfandel (58%), Petite Sirah (25%), and Carignan (17%). This Petite Sirah presence is significant—Petite Sirah was widely used as a blending grape in old-vine Napa vineyards to add color, structure, and aging potential to the softer Zinfandel. Stony loam, alluvial fans, volcanic-influenced soils. Base of Mt. St. Helena. Dry-farmed.

name: Rous Vineyard
raw_text: Located in the heart of the Russian River Valley, the Rous Vineyard sits on Goldridge sandy loam soils—the benchmark soil type for this appellation. The old-vine field blend is dominated by Zinfandel (72%) with Petite Sirah (13%), Carignan (8%), and other varieties (7%) making up the balance. The cool climate, morning fog, and Goldridge soils create wines of elegance and spice rather than sheer power. Goldridge sandy loam soils. Marine-influenced climate. Morning fog. Russian River cooling effect.
